messages:
samir: heads-up — starting micro-canary for rate-policy v3.1 at 15:00 UTC. This is a very small slice (0.3%). We'll raise burst_limit by 20% for backend connections only. Will monitor 429/latency. ian, if you see anything weird please ping.

clare: ack. Will watch support queue. Any specific customers we need to exclude from this micro-canary?

samir: good Q — exclude enterprise customers tagged with `tier:enterprise` and any sessions with `session:dedicated`. Config patch: `route.selector != enterprise && session != dedicated`.

matt: quick note from infra — the autoscaler will still treat the canary pool as part of the pool, so metric spikes might cause extra nodes. If we want to keep capacity flat, we should set `autoscale.min=canary.nodes` manual. Do we want that?

kira: prefer not to add manual ops. We'll set a soft cap: `autoscale.bias=0.2` for the canary. Also enabling prefix cache for the canary to reduce repeated KVs.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rate-policy/v3.1 -> canary (0.3%). rollout_id=roll-2024-11-05-15-00

samir: noticed from the first 3 mins: small uptick in 429s from internal e2e tests hitting the canary. Numbers: 429 rate ~0.9% vs baseline 0.05%. No customer-facing errors reported yet. Logs:

```
[2024-11-05T15:03:12Z] req_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate status=429 reason=burst_limit_exceeded policy=rate-policy-v3.1 bucket=canary
[2024-11-05T15:03:12Z] svc=frontier latency_ms=24
```

clare: support queue has two tickets from dev accounts showing 429 around 15:03. Both dev keys are in the canary bucket. I'm triaging now but marking as P2 for now.

matt: can someone confirm whether the canary was configured to apply higher burst limits only on generate endpoints? If the change hit embeddings/streaming that could be a mismatch.

kira: good catch — policy patch was scoped to routes matching `/v1/*` but the regex accidentally matched embeddings routes too. Fixing now to target `/v1/generate` only. Pushing patch.

deploy-bot: rollout update: patch applied, targeting refined route. rollout_id=roll-2024-11-05-15-00 update=scope-fix

samir: after scope fix, 429 rate dropped to 0.12% and trending down. Latency stable. Observability graphs: 1-min and 5-min.

clare: closing the two dev tickets with note that it was canary config scope; flagged customers excluded. Adding repro steps to internal KB.

support-bot: note added to incident-log: "micro-canary rate-policy v3.1 produced transient 429s due to overbroad route match; fixed by scoping to /v1/generate; impact: dev keys only; action: rollback if >1% 429 sustained for 10m."

matt: recommend we keep canary running for another 30m with increased sampling (to 1%) to ensure no second-order effects from prefix cache change. samir — can we bump to 1% for 30m and set automatic rollback threshold 429>0.5% for 5m?

samir: 👍 bumped to 1% for 30m. Auto-rollback set to: if 429_rate > 0.5 for 300s then rollback. Deploy details: `kubectl patch rollout roll-2024-11-05-15-00 --patch '{"spec": {"canaryPercent": 1}}'`

kira: monitoring hooks in console: added alert panel to the canary dashboard and updated the SLO annotations.

clare: FYI — I updated the KB with repro steps and the fix. Repro: hit canary with parallel clients 50x from a dev key, you'll see early 429s if route mis-scope exists. I'll add the test script to the repo.

matt: thanks all. If auto-rollback fires, ops will run the rollback playbook and notify @oncall. Otherwise we'll proceed to staged rollout tomorrow. Good catch on the regex.

samir: closing loop. Great teamwork. :heart:
